documentTitle: Four pillars, nineteen themes — ADEB LONODJI
description: How ADEB LONODJI organises its work: four pillars, nineteen themes and two cross-cutting units, each set against the UN Sustainable Development Goals it touches.
title: Four pillars, nineteen themes
lede: ADEB LONODJI organises its work into nineteen themes grouped in four pillars, supported by two cross-cutting units. Each theme is meant to be led by a coordinator who reports to the membership. This page is the English summary; every theme has a fuller description en français .

sections.html:
Before the list

Six coordinators out of nineteen

We would rather say this plainly than let a well-ordered table suggest otherwise: thirteen of the nineteen themes have no coordinator today. The structure below is what the association has decided to build, not what it already runs. If you are a Bedjond professional, in Chad or in the diaspora, and one of these themes is your field, write to us.

At target level the answer is more qualified, and we would rather give it ourselves: our themes carry forty-two of the one hundred and sixty-nine targets, and four targets central to development are still not among them. We do not claim child stunting (2.2), adult literacy (4.6), child labour (8.7) or the cost of diaspora remittances (10.c). For a rural territory in southern Chad these are front-rank issues, and two of them are already listed among the local problems we track. But none of our themes has put them on its programme, and we will not display a target nobody is working on. Those four are open pieces of work — if one of them matters to you, tell us.

Each theme is set against the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals it actually touches — two or three, no more. For each goal we also give the precise target number: the seventeen goals break down into one hundred and sixty-nine targets, and that is the level at which a mapping means anything — “SDG 5” says nothing, “target 5.2, eliminate violence against women and girls” says exactly what is meant. Hover a badge for the full wording. That alignment is our own reading, not a label awarded by anyone, and it can be corrected.

Gender & Women’s Empowerment

Coordinator: Odette Tolmbaye

Women’s empowerment, income-generating groups, leadership training, and an effective presence of women in the association’s own governing bodies. The theme also carries the fight against gender-based violence: domestic violence, forced marriage, imposed levirate and abusive widowhood rites, harassment at school. Chad passed an ordinance in 2025 that punishes these acts heavily — up to ten years’ imprisonment for a forced marriage — and almost no one knows it exists: making it known is already an action.

Health & Prevention

Coordinator: Dr Nestor Alladoumdjim

Prevention campaigns, liaison with health centres, the fight against alcohol abuse — adulterated alcohol above all — and hygiene and sanitation. The theme rests on a published health advocacy brief, tracked indicator by indicator: a maternity unit working day and night with a qualified midwife, a reliable cold chain for childhood vaccination, a basic laboratory to diagnose malaria, typhoid and tuberculosis, an ambulance and an evacuation protocol. Targets 3.1, 3.2 and 3.3 answer to that file, not to an intention.

Social Protection & Inclusion

Coordinator: Solkem Ngarmbatina

A mutual-aid fund for bereavement and illness, emergency support, and particular attention to widows and people with disabilities. With Entrepreneurship & Inclusive Finance, this is the association’s anti-poverty theme — not as a slogan, but as a safety net where a death, an illness or a failed harvest tips a whole family over.
